status: one-seed z-only conditioning-mechanism diagnostic; not a headline result
interpretation: Prefix-style conditioning is the first non-additive mechanism tested in the z-only setting.

On this one-seed held-out pilot it is competitive with the best additive late-layer schedule: exact match is slightly lower (.162 versus .164), facet satisfaction is slightly higher (.624 versus .619), and the shuffled-goal effect is slightly higher (.057 versus .055).
Because held-out probe accuracy remains similar, the difference again appears to come from how generation uses the latent rather than from a large change in decodability.
The current evidence therefore supports two viable directions for the next stage: selective late additive access and continuous prefix conditioning.
